newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders eye EU wheat export refund around 19 Ecus.
newsitem.headline: Traders eye EU wheat export refund around 19 Ecus.

text.p: Several grain exporters on Thursday said they were expecting the European Union to grant a refund of around 19 Ecus per tonne to export free-market soft wheat at this week's grain auction.
This would allow the release of up to 172,000 tonnes of wheat in France, plus any additional tonnages granted elsewhere in the EU, they said.
But exporters were unsure the European Commission was ready to substantially step up its wheat export refund from the 14.98 Ecus granted the previous week.
In France grain traders bid to export 421,750 tonnes of European Union soft wheat at rebates ranging from 17.37 to 22.98 Ecus per tonne.
Last week the European Union granted the export of 249,800 tonnes of soft wheat at a maximum rebate of 14.98 Ecus.
The lowest wheat export refund offer placed in France was for the export of 3,000 tonnes of wheat, traders said.

Other offers included bids to export up to 55,000 tonnes of wheat with a refund of 18.25 Ecus, 109,000 tonnes at 18.50 Ecus, 172,000 tonnes at 19.00 Ecus, 224,000 tonnes at 20.00 Ecus and up to 421,750 tonnes at 22.98 Ecus.
Traders suggested some exporters might be trying to help cover part of a large sale of French wheat to Egypt although they stressed exporters did not bid for very substantial export volumes.

One exporter suggested that some operators who sold wheat to Egypt might have done so with their long positions and were simply trying to grab new licences. A few operators might be testing the Commission's willingness to step up refunds.
Last weekend France sold a total of 500,000 tonnes of soft wheat to Egypt at prices ranging from $140.50 to $143.90 Ecus per tonne, Fob.
Traders estimated the EU needed to hike last week's refund by three to four Ecus to cover the Egyptian sale.

They said the EU might not be prepared to grant immediately refunds sufficient to cover the sale, but that it could not afford to miss what could be one of the last substantial sales of old crop wheat in the current season.
